title.value: CulturAdaptEval: Do Language Models Get You? A Dual-Axis Benchmark for Cultural Empathy in Multicultural Dialogue

abstract.value:
Large Language Models (LLMs) are no longer just text generators—they are
companions, advisors, and interlocutors embedded in daily life. But do they truly
get the people they serve? Prior work has studied empathy and cultural adaptation
separately, but never in tandem. We introduce EXACT (Empathy × Culture
Assessment of Conversational Tasks), the first framework for evaluating cultural
empathy in dialogue. EXACT combines (i) a dual-axis benchmark of 504 culturally
situated scenarios—spanning 12 globally grounded personas (e.g., a South Indian
student ashamed of disappointing her family) and 6 core emotional states (e.g.,
grief, shame, guilt, spiritual doubt)—with (ii) a robustness-first evaluation protocol
that integrates multi-family ensemble judges, order randomization with flip-check
filtering, verbosity controls, and Bradley–Terry–Luce modeling with bootstrap
confidence intervals.
We evaluated 14 state-of-the-art LLMs across multiple providers and anchor
automated scores with a targeted human validation study using Best–Worst Scaling,
strategically oversampling ambiguous cases, and key model rivalries. Our findings
reveal stark cultural blind spots, emotion-dependent empathy failures, and rank
inversions between pooled and macro-averaged scores, challenging the notion of a
single “best” model. All prompts, generations, and evaluation code are released to
catalyze the development of culturally aligned AI.
